title: When Accelerometer Roll Estimation Fails: The Pitch Singularity

attitude.regularized_roll_deg: atan2(a_y, copysign(1, a_z) * sqrt(a_z^2 + mu * a_x^2))
attitude.computed: on-target, by the firmware, and recorded as the attitude_deg and attitude_reg_deg channels

regularization.note: The subscript in attitude_reg_deg[i] is an index into the firmware's mu table, not a value. The order is NOT monotone: [1] is the strongest regularization and [4] the weakest. mu = 0 in [0] is the unregularized estimate.

captures.purpose: board rotated to vertical and back, driving pitch to -89.4° so the roll estimate loses its input
captures.notes: |pitch| exceeds 85° between 13.8 s and 21.9 s. a_z changes sign from 16.30 s onwards, where every estimate correctly reports a real change of orientation rather than noise.

captures.purpose: ordinary hand-held movement well away from the singularity, showing what regularization costs at everyday angles
captures.notes: Compare these channels on the median, not the peak. The peak deviation is 2.7° for every coefficient including mu = 0.0001, which is inter-channel sampling skew and not regularization error.

notes: The sensor samples at 1 kHz. Samples reach the host over SWD at roughly 280/s in these captures, which is the polling rate of the acquisition and not a property of the sensor.

Each variable is read in its own SWD transaction, so two channels recorded in the same row can come from firmware iterations a millisecond apart. attitude_deg.roll and attitude_reg_deg[0].roll are the same quantity computed twice on-target and still differ by a median of about 0.06° for this reason.
Only attitude_reg_deg[0] carries a pitch channel. Regularization changes the roll formula alone, so the other four would be identical copies of it.
